subject: Transition from PAYG to Committed Private Offer — governance & pricing clause
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@catalyst.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Moving from PAYG to committed private offer — initial info and ask

Hi Marcus / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demos last week — the infra and cost story look promising. We're ready to commit to a private offer on AWS, moving off PAYG, and procurement asked me to send the high-level ask so you can prepare the private-offer paperwork. Topline: 12-month committed term starting 2026-11-01, committed throughput equivalent to ~1.2M inference tokens/month (we've included a rough run-rate), billing on a monthly invoice but open to a quarterly tranche if that's standard.

A few governance/contract items procurement wants flagged up front so legal can review concurrently:
- We want an explicit cap on mid-term price increases: any price change should be limited to CPI or agreed schedules (we call this out as the "no-surprise price" ask).
- Can you confirm data residency and logging for audit (SOC2 evidence requested)?
- We've also got a marketplace requirement around the seller's right to change listing terms (they call it an "auction clause") — procurement would prefer either removal or a narrow carve that prevents unilateral price changes mid-commitment.

I've attached our procurement checklist (procurement will send a signed PO once we have the DocuSign link and PO-ready line items). Can someone from your side confirm the canonical line items you need on the PO (model SKU / committed units / start date / billing cadence) and whether Redwood will issue a marketplace private-offer link for DocuSign?

Thanks,
Sara

-----
Sara Li
Head of Platform Ops, Catalyst AI
sara.li@catalyst.ai
(415) 555-0123
Attachment: catalyst_procurement_checklist.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@catalyst.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Moving from PAYG to committed private offer — initial info and ask

Hi Sara — great to hear you're ready to commit. Copying Kimberly from our Marketplace/Enterprise team so she can surface the exact PO line items and get legal looped. Quick answers below so procurement has what they need immediately: 

1) Canonical PO line items: we typically include a single committed SKU (REW-CORE-COMMIT) + committed units (tokens/month) + term start/end + agreed billing cadence. We can provide the exact text for each line so it maps cleanly to AWS private-offer fields.

2) DocuSign / marketplace flow: yes — we generate the private-offer in the marketplace and provide the DocuSign/acceptance link. We also support a separate vendor PO if you need Redwood invoicing directly (we'll need your billing contact + tax info for that).

3) Auction clause / price-change: low friction to include language that prevents unilateral price increases for the duration of the committed term. Our legal typically proposes a narrow exception for changes driven by newly imposed taxes or regulatory fees, and we can cap other changes to CPI + x%. Kimberly, can you propose the standard clause we use?

Next steps from our side: Kimberly will drop the PO template and the private-offer creation timeline. If procurement can confirm whether they prefer monthly or quarterly billing (and whether they will provide a vendor PO), we can get DocuSign out within 3 business days of sign-off.

Best,
Marcus

Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@catalyst.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Moving from PAYG to committed private offer — initial info and ask

Hi Sara / Marcus / Ben — attaching the PO template and a simple commit calculation workbook so procurement can see how we map tokens -> committed units and pricing. Key notes: 
- We can structure invoicing monthly or quarterly. If you want smoother cash flow, quarterly tranches are common for 12-month terms.
- For marketplace private offers we need: legal signatory name, billing email, billing address, and a primary PO number (if Catalyst will use an external PO).
- Regarding the auction clause: our standard language prevents unilateral price increases during a locked committed term; I'll paste the clause below and attach a redline option for legal.

[Standard Price Protection Clause]
"Seller will not increase per-unit pricing for the committed SKU during the term except as required by changes in applicable taxes or regulatory fees. Any other proposed price changes require mutual written agreement and 90 days' notice."

If Catalyst legal wants an explicit CPI cap we can add: "Price increases, if any, will be limited to CPI + 1.0% per annum." Let me know which option they'd prefer and we will push that into the private-offer.

Attaching: commit_calculation.xlsx, po_template_private_offer.docx

Ben — can you confirm the AWS marketplace creation window and whether we need any additional metadata for Catalyst's account to ensure the private-offer maps to their org in AWS?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Marketplace Sales Operations
kimberly.park@redwood.com
Attachment: commit_calculation.xlsx; po_template_private_offer.docx

From: procurement@catalyst.ai <procurement@catalyst.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@catalyst.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Catalyst PO (signed) + DocuSign link — please confirm mapping and next steps

Marcus / Kimberly,

Please find attached our signed PO for the 12-month commitment (start 2026-11-01). We opted for monthly invoicing. A few housekeeping items: 
- Attached file: Catalyst_PO_signed.pdf (signed by our CFO)
- DocuSign acceptance link: https://www.docusign.com/en/projects/abc123456 (we will accept via your private-offer link)
- Regarding the price-change language: our legal accepted the "Standard Price Protection Clause" you proposed, they asked that the exception for taxes be explicitly called out.

Next steps requested on your side: 
1) Confirm the final private-offer SKU and committed unit numbers so we can accept in the marketplace.
2) Confirm Redwood's billing contact and whether Redwood will issue monthly invoices to our AP team (ap@catalyst.ai) or whether invoices come via AWS marketplace billing.
3) Provide the DocuSign/private-offer link and expected timeline to have the private-offer active in the marketplace.

Thanks,
Catalyst Procurement
procurement@catalyst.ai
Attachment: Catalyst_PO_signed.pdf
